description: Example FR-16 evaluation set over six well-known ML papers. Page numbers refer to the published PDFs and MUST be verified against your own copies before trusting a score: an off-by-one page label turns a correct retrieval into a counted miss. Replace this file with questions and labels from your own library for a result that means anything to you. Tags exist so a report can be sliced by question type — 'exact-term' (model, dataset and author names) is where reranking and keyword search are easiest to regress.

cases.question: In the Transformer, how is multi-head attention computed and why is it used instead of a single attention head?

expected_pages.note: Section 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention / 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention
MultiHead formula and the 'different positions' argument

expected_answer_characteristics: states that each head is a separate projection followed by a concatenation and linear layer
gives the multi-head formula or describes concatenating h parallel attention heads
explains that different heads can attend to different positions or subspaces

cases.question: What BLEU scores does the paper report for its base and big Transformer models on WMT 2014 English-to-German?
expected_answer_characteristics: reports a number together with its unit or benchmark name
distinguishes the base model from the big model
does not invent a score for a split that is not in the table

cases.question: In RAG, how does the retrieved document enter the generation step?

expected_pages.paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

expected_answer_characteristics: describes concatenating or marginalising a latent document representation with the query representation
mentions marginalising over the retrieved documents rather than conditioning on one
distinguishes the generator from the retriever

cases.question: How does BERT choose its masked language modelling tokens, and what percentage does it mask?

expected_pages.paper_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
expected_pages.note: Section 3.1.1 Masked LM, including the 15% figure

expected_answer_characteristics: states the masking rate as 15% of tokens
explains that of the masked tokens 80% are replaced with [MASK], 10% with a random token, and 10% are left unchanged
does not confuse the rate of selection with the rate of replacement

cases.question: What problem does the DenseNet layer design solve, and what is the compression factor?

expected_pages.note: Section 3.1 DenseNet layer / 3.2 compression, and Table 1 for the compression factor

expected_answer_characteristics: identifies the alleviation of vanishing gradients or optimisation difficulty from shorter connections
describes transition layers as reducing the number of feature maps

cases.question: In the Adam optimizer paper, how are the running averages of the gradients decayed, and what are the default beta values?

expected_pages.paper_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
expected_pages.note: Section 2.1 Algorithm, equations for m and v with beta1 and beta2

expected_answer_characteristics: gives the bias-corrected exponential moving averages for the first and second moments
states the default beta1 = 0.9 and beta2 = 0.999
notes that alpha corrects the bias from the zero initialisation, not that it is a learning rate decay
